title: Novalex POC scoping - workload & benchmarks
next_steps: Redwood to run 24h synthetic benchmark with Novalex sample workload (SE-led)
Customer to share 1k representative prompts + expected labels by 2026-03-30
Schedule kickoff for week of 2026-03-30 to provision Dedicated test pool if needed
Redwood to share SOC2 & network/VPC checklist and benchmark spreadsheet
action_items: Daniel Kim: Prepare benchmark config and load scripts : 2026-03-29
Liam O'Connor: Share sample prompt set and per-endpoint QPS targets : 2026-03-30
Sofia Martinez: Send pricing sketch and POC SOW draft : 2026-04-01
summary: POC scoping call to align on workload characterization and traffic modeling for Novalex's summarization and Q&A endpoints. Main goals: agree success criteria (latency p95/throughput), provide representative workload (QPS, concurrency, token distributions), run Redwood benchmark vs production-like traffic, and define timeline for a 2-week POC. Security and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) discussed; customer leans toward dedicated if latency/SLAs need it.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost)
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-25 15:00 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Novalex CTO), Liam O'Connor (Novalex Head of MLOps), Priya Patel (Novalex Platform)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - I'm Sofia, AE on the Redwood side, with Daniel our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: Good, thanks. We've been looking forward to this.
[00:12] Daniel: Hi all - quick agenda: scoping the POC, understanding your workload (QPS, concurrency, token sizes), defining success criteria, and planning benchmarks. We'll also cover deployment/security needs.
[00:24] Priya: Sounds good. We're primarily focused on two endpoints: a real-time Q&A flow for our app and a longer document summarization pipeline used in async batch jobs.
[00:35] Sofia: Perfect. Can you share rough traffic numbers and SLOs for each?
[00:40] Liam: For the Q&A endpoint, we see peaks ~10 QPS per region, sustained around 4 QPS. Concurrency on the backend is typically 8-12 active sessions; but burst to 20 is possible during marketing campaigns. Latency SLO we're targeting is p95 under 300ms for short prompts - maybe aggressive, but that's the goal.
[01:05] Daniel: Ok that's helpful. What are your average token sizes for Q&A? Input and output?
[01:10] Priya: Avg input ~60 tokens, output ~120 tokens. But there's a tail: some queries include snips of context up to 600 tokens. For summarization, inputs can be 1k-2k tokens and outputs typically 200-400 tokens.
[01:28] Sofia: Got it. So two distinct workloads: real-time low-token low-latency and batch high-token summarization. For the POC we should model both. Does Novalex want Redwood to run synthetic load or do you prefer to run tests from your env hitting our hosted endpoints?
[01:44] Aisha: We prefer Redwood to run the initial synthetic benchmark using our prompt set to reduce setup overhead, but we will also want an end-to-end test from our staging app later.
[01:54] Daniel: That's fine. We'll ask for a representative sample of 1,000 prompts for each flow - helps us model token distributions and QPS patterns. We usually run a 24-48 hour synthetic run to capture steady-state and burst behavior.
[02:07] Liam: Cool. For throughput, the QPS target for the POC should reflect our regional peaks, so please test up to 20 QPS with bursts and a steady-state of 6 QPS. For summarization, we'll measure tokens/sec and cost.
[02:22] Sofia: Success criteria - what matters most? Latency p95, cost per 1M tokens, and quality metrics (answer accuracy / ROUGE for summarization)?
[02:31] Aisha: Exactly. We need p95 latency below 400ms for Q&A in the POC to consider hosted; if not, we'll look at Dedicated. Also, quality must match our current OpenAI results - for summarization we have automated ROUGE/L-based checks and a manual sample of ~200 prompts.
[02:50] Daniel: We'll run automated quality evals against your label set. For latency, note that short prompts are sensitive to cold starts and batching - we can test 0-batch (no batching) and batching modes. Also, KV cache/prefix caching can help for repeated queries; we'll model that too.
[03:10] Priya: On caching - how do you handle KV cache across Dedicated vs Hosted? We have multi-tenant concerns and data residency.
[03:17] Daniel: For Hosted we have tenant isolation at the request level and per-route caching options; for Dedicated you get isolated GPU pools and optionally local caching with customer-managed VPC. For KMS and encryption at rest we integrate with customer KMS in the Private deployment.
[03:33] Liam: We'll need SOC2 documentation and network diagrams. Also SSO/SAML for our admins.
[03:38] Sofia: We'll send SOC2, ISO checklist, and the VPC networking runbook. I'll add that as an action item.
[03:44] Aisha: Great. Can you talk about what metrics you'll provide post-benchmark?
[03:49] Daniel: We'll deliver a benchmark report with p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, request/sec, cost estimates per 1M tokens, and a quality score versus your labeled set. We'll also include suggestions - batching profiles, quantization recommendations, and whether Dedicated capacity is warranted.
[04:07] Priya: For cost estimation, make sure you include both token costs and GPU-hours for Dedicated. We need to justify to finance.
[04:15] Daniel: Absolutely. We'll provide cost delta scenarios: hosted per-token vs reserved Dedicated pool (monthly) with burst pricing.
[04:23] Sofia: Timeline proposal: Kickoff next week (week of 2026-03-30), Redwood runs initial synthetic benchmark within first week, then a two-week POC where we optionally provision a short-lived Dedicated pool if needed. Does that fit your expectations?
[04:38] Liam: Yes. We want benchmark results before committing to Dedicated. Also want to run a quality review with 200 human-evaluated prompts during the POC.
[04:47] Aisha: On data: we'll scrub sensitive PII from prompts but will need to confirm data retention settings - don't persist logs beyond X days unless needed for debugging. Is that configurable?
[04:58] Daniel: Yes, retention policies are configurable; for Hosted we can set shorter retention and redact logs; Dedicated/Private provides more controls and local log retention. We'll share the retention options doc.
[05:10] Priya: Any gotchas about long inputs for summarization? We have some 2k token docs - do you rely on chunking or extended context models?
[05:18] Daniel: Two options: chunk + summarize then combine (pipeline) or use long-context variants; each has tradeoffs in latency and quality. We'll model both approaches in the POC: measure end-to-end latency and quality.
[05:31] Sofia: Are there any external services or integrations needed for Novalex during POC?
[05:35] Liam: We'll need connectivity for our staging VPC to Redwood's test endpoints if we do the direct staging test. Also access to our sample dataset in S3.
[05:43] Daniel: We can secure test credentials and temporary IAM roles. We'll provide guidance in the network checklist.
[05:49] Aisha: Benchmarks - what do you consider a fair synthetic traffic pattern?
[05:53] Daniel: We use a mix: steady-state at 60% of peak for 12h, randomized bursts to 100% peak for short windows, and tail-heavy token size distribution based on your sample. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and config.
[06:07] Priya: Can Redwood simulate session affinity? Our Q&A clients maintain short lived sessions with context windows that grow.
[06:13] Daniel: Yes, we can simulate session behavior with growing prefix sizes which will exercise KV cache. That helps show cost savings and latency improvements.
[06:21] Sofia: Any questions on acceptance criteria?
[06:24] Aisha: One: if p95 is slightly above target but quality is better than current provider, are you flexible on pass/fail?
[06:31] Sofia: We recommend a weighted acceptance: latency (40%), quality (40%), cost (20%). We can bake that into the SOW.
[06:41] Liam: OK. For reporting cadence during POC - weekly syncs?
[06:45] Sofia: Weekly check-ins, plus mid-benchmark adhoc when we see anomalies.
[06:49] Daniel: We'll kick-off with a short run to validate config, then run the 24-48h full run, then the two-week eval with human labeling.
[06:57] Priya: Anything else on infra sizing? For Dedicated, what GPU class do you recommend for our load?
[07:02] Daniel: Based on initial numbers (20 QPS bursts, avg tokens), medium sized T4-like instances could work for cost, but for low p95 latency we'd recommend A100 or H100 class for summaries if you want fastest p95s. We'll produce a sizing matrix in the report.
[07:18] Sofia: We'll include recommended quantization and batching settings; sometimes int8 quantization is enough for summarization workloads with little quality hit.
[07:26] Aisha: Ok good. Next steps recap?
[07:29] Sofia: Recap: 1) Liam share prompt sets + QPS targets by 2026-03-30; 2) Daniel prepares benchmark config and runs initial synthetic run (by 2026-03-29); 3) Sofia sends SOW/pricing and SOC2 + network docs (by 2026-04-01); 4) Schedule kickoff for week of 2026-03-30.
[07:51] Aisha: That's right. One more thing - can you include a column in the benchmark sheet for 'expected user-visible latency' vs internal tokens/sec? Helps our PMs.
[07:59] Daniel: Will do.
[08:02] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email with links to the benchmark spreadsheet and the SOC2 pack.
[08:08] Liam: Thanks all.
[08:10] Aisha: Thanks.

Notes: occasional transcription errors - e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache; "H-one hundred" misheard for H100 in a couple places. References shared: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/novalex-spreadsheet (benchmark spreadsheet), SOC2 packet link (sent after call).

End of transcript.
